categories.main_business_segments: TOC Co., Ltd. operates primarily in two business segments: real estate (property leasing, management, and operation of office buildings, commercial facilities, exhibition halls, and parking lots) and linen supply & laundry services (mainly for hotels). The group also engages in ancillary businesses such as pharmaceutical manufacturing and sales, sports clubs, spa facilities, building management services, and information processing.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core operations rely on property management expertise, efficient building maintenance, and tenant services. In the linen supply segment, industrial-scale laundry and supply chain management are key. The pharmaceutical business utilizes standard pharmaceutical manufacturing and quality control processes. Facility upgrades focus on energy efficiency, disaster resilience, and environmental sustainability.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include corporate tenants (offices and retail), hotels (for linen supply), and consumers using sports clubs, spas, and commercial facilities. The real estate segment serves a broad range of industries seeking office or retail space, while the linen supply business primarily targets the hospitality sector.
categories.geographic_coverage: Operations are concentrated in the Tokyo metropolitan area, with all major properties and facilities located in central Tokyo (Shinagawa, Taito, Koto, Sumida, Minato wards) and some in Kanagawa (Atsugi). The company does not have significant overseas operations.
categories.supply_chain_position: TOC operates downstream in the supply chain, directly providing real estate leasing, facility management, and end-user services. In linen supply, it acts as a service provider to hotels and related businesses. The pharmaceutical segment is vertically integrated, handling manufacturing and sales.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include maximizing the value and occupancy of owned properties, enhancing operational efficiency, and pursuing high-value-added services. The company emphasizes sustainability, disaster resilience, and energy efficiency in property management. There is no significant R&D activity, but ongoing investments are made in facility upgrades and environmental initiatives.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is primarily generated through rental income from office, retail, and commercial properties, as well as service fees from linen supply, laundry, sports clubs, and spas. The pharmaceutical segment earns revenue from product sales. Building management and ancillary services provide additional fee-based income.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: TOC competes with other major Japanese real estate developers and property management firms in the Tokyo metropolitan area, as well as specialized linen supply companies and local fitness/spa operators. The company positions itself as a stable, asset-heavy landlord with a focus on high-occupancy, multi-use properties and value-added services.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ended March 2025, consolidated revenue was 13.15 billion yen, with operating profit of 1.42 billion yen and net profit attributable to shareholders of 1.79 billion yen. The company has a high equity ratio (87.2%) and total assets of 114.9 billion yen. Recent years have seen declining revenue and profit due to temporary building closures and tenant turnover, but the company maintains a stable financial base.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: TOC emphasizes stable, long-term value creation through ownership and management of large-scale, multi-purpose properties in prime Tokyo locations. The company differentiates itself by offering integrated services (leasing, management, event spaces, and amenities), high occupancy rates, and a commitment to sustainability and disaster resilience. Its diversified service portfolio (including linen supply and wellness facilities) adds further value for tenants and customers.
